metadata.description: Pattern Recognition, Feature Selection unit, KP04 ROC curve and AUC; guided v1; English self-study; answer first then feedback

scene-u01.name: Pattern Recognition: Feature Selection KP04 ROC Curve and AUC

p01-overlap-title.name: p01-overlap-title
p01-overlap-title.text: Means can differ and the two classes still blur together: what we measure is the overlap

p01-overlap-ctx.name: p01-overlap-ctx
p01-overlap-ctx.text: The test of KP03 looks only at "how much the means differ". The overlap of the two classes needs the whole distribution.

p01-overlap-lo.name: p01-overlap-lo
p01-overlap-lo.text: Red = the overlapping part of the two classes

p01-overlap-ct.name: p01-overlap-ct
p01-overlap-ct.text: A large mean gap does not mean small overlap; the more overlap, the easier any decision using this feature goes wrong

p02-threshold-title.name: p02-threshold-title
p02-threshold-title.text: One threshold, two errors, trading off

p02-threshold-ctx.name: p02-threshold-ctx
p02-threshold-ctx.text: A value above $t$ is labelled $\omega_2$, otherwise $\omega_1$. Put $t$ at $1$:

p02-threshold-tr.name: p02-threshold-tr
p02-threshold-tr.text: Move the threshold right: false alarms ($\alpha$) fall and misses ($\beta$) rise; move it left and it is the opposite; no position makes both smallest at once

p03-counts-title.name: p03-counts-title
p03-counts-title.text: Compute $(\alpha,\ 1-\beta)$ from counts: one threshold is one point in the plane

p03-counts-ctx.name: p03-counts-ctx
p03-counts-ctx.text: 100 samples: 50 of $\omega_1$ and 50 of $\omega_2$. The result after setting one threshold.

p04-sweep-title.name: p04-sweep-title
p04-sweep-title.text: Sweep all thresholds and the points join into the ROC curve

p04-sweep-ctx.name: p04-sweep-ctx
p04-sweep-ctx.text: Left: the two class distributions and three thresholds; right: the dots of the same colour are the $(\alpha,\ 1-\beta)$ of these three thresholds.

p04-sweep-auc.name: p04-sweep-auc
p04-sweep-auc.text: Area under the curve $\mathrm{AUC}=0.921$: the two class means are $2\sigma$ apart

p05-hand-title.name: p05-hand-title
p05-hand-title.text: Hand-computed ROC of 12 values: count once per threshold

p05-hand-ctx.name: p05-hand-ctx
p05-hand-ctx.text: 6 values each for $\omega_1$ and $\omega_2$; put a threshold at the midpoint of each pair of neighbours.

p05-hand-sc0.name: p05-hand-sc0
p05-hand-sc0.text:
Threshold $3.45$: on the right there are
3 of $\omega_1$, 5 of $\omega_2$
$\alpha=\frac{3}{6}=0.500$, $1-\beta=\frac{5}{6}=0.833$

p05-hand-sc1.name: p05-hand-sc1
p05-hand-sc1.text:
Threshold $4.40$: on the right there are
1 of $\omega_1$, 4 of $\omega_2$
$\alpha=\frac{1}{6}=0.167$, $1-\beta=\frac{4}{6}=0.667$

p06-area-title.name: p06-area-title
p06-area-title.text: AUC: the area under the staircase; only the part above the diagonal is discriminating power

p06-area-ctx.name: p06-area-ctx
p06-area-ctx.text: The area under the diagonal is $0.5$ (guessing). Complete separation gives $1$.

p06-area-a1.name: p06-area-a1
p06-area-a1.text:
Area under the diagonal $=\dfrac12=0.5$
(guessing, the two classes overlap completely)

p06-area-a2.name: p06-area-a2
p06-area-a2.text: Area between the staircase and the diagonal $=0.833-0.5=0.333$

p06-area-a3.name: p06-area-a3
p06-area-a3.text:
$\mathrm{AUC}=\dfrac12+0.333=0.833$
(the textbook measures the "area between the curve and the diagonal", from $0$ to $\frac12$)

p07-pairs-title.name: p07-pairs-title
p07-pairs-title.text: Meaning of AUC: pick one of each at random; how often is $\omega_2$ larger?

p07-pairs-ctx.name: p07-pairs-ctx
p07-pairs-ctx.text: There are $6\times6=36$ pairs = the 36 cells below. Each cell is a pair $(\omega_1,\ \omega_2)$; green = the value of $\omega_2$ is larger.

p07-pairs-pbt.name: p07-pairs-pbt
p07-pairs-pbt.text: 36 cells = 36 pairings; how many are green?

p07-pairs-eq.name: p07-pairs-eq
p07-pairs-eq.text:
Same as the area under the staircase: $0.833$
roc_auc_score of scikit-learn also gives 0.8333

p07-pairs-mean.name: p07-pairs-mean
p07-pairs-mean.text:
Meaning: draw one $\omega_1$ and one $\omega_2$ at random;
the probability that the value of $\omega_2$ is larger $=$ AUC

p08-gauss-title.name: p08-gauss-title
p08-gauss-title.text: Better separation bulges the curve to the upper left: $\mathrm{AUC}=\Phi(\Delta/(\sigma\sqrt2))$

p08-gauss-ctx.name: p08-gauss-ctx
p08-gauss-ctx.text: When both classes are normal with equal variance, AUC depends only on how many standard deviations the mean gap is.

p08-gauss-rlg.name: p08-gauss-rlg
p08-gauss-rlg.text: Legend: curve colour = how many standard deviations apart the two class means are

p08-gauss-fm.name: p08-gauss-fm
p08-gauss-fm.text: $\mathrm{AUC}=\Phi\!\left(\dfrac{\Delta}{\sigma\sqrt2}\right)$: at $\Delta=0$ it hugs the diagonal ($0.5$); at $\Delta=3\sigma$ it is $0.983$

p09-kp03-title.name: p09-kp03-title
p09-kp03-title.text: Back to KP03: the $p$-value is significant, yet the AUC is only a little better than guessing

p09-kp03-ctx.name: p09-kp03-ctx
p09-kp03-ctx.text: 500 samples per class (teaching setup, seed 0), with a true mean gap of only $0.2\sigma$.

p09-kp03-au.name: p09-kp03-au
p09-kp03-au.text:
AUC $=0.544$
Only slightly better than random guessing (0.5)

p09-kp03-ms.name: p09-kp03-ms
p09-kp03-ms.text: The $p$-value answers "do the means differ?"; the AUC answers "how well do the classes separate?"; two different questions

p10-samegap-title.name: p10-samegap-title
p10-samegap-title.text: The same mean gap with different spread gives very different AUC

p10-samegap-ctx.name: p10-samegap-ctx
p10-samegap-ctx.text: Both features have a mean gap of $3$. Feature A has $\sigma=1$ and feature B has $\sigma=3$.

p10-samegap-ct.name: p10-samegap-ct
p10-samegap-ct.text: Same mean gap, very different AUC: the larger the spread, the more overlap; FDR also divides the mean gap by the spread (KP05)

p11-samemean-title.name: p11-samemean-title
p11-samemean-title.text: A blind spot of ROC: same mean, different spread; a one-sided threshold sees no discriminating power

p11-samemean-ctx.name: p11-samemean-ctx
p11-samemean-ctx.text: $\omega_1\sim N(0,1)$, $\omega_2\sim N(0,3^2)$: the narrow blue hill sits on top of the wide gold hill.

p11-samemean-ct.name: p11-samemean-ct
p11-samemean-ct.text: ROC assumes a "one-sided threshold"; when the discriminating power hides in another form (how far from the centre), change the feature representation first, then compute AUC

p12-practice1-title.name: p12-practice1-title
p12-practice1-title.text: Exercise 1: compute a point on the ROC from counts

p12-practice1-ctx.name: p12-practice1-ctx
p12-practice1-ctx.text: Work it out yourself first, then press Next for feedback.

p12-practice1-q1.name: p12-practice1-q1
p12-practice1-q1.text: Exercise 1: two classes with 20 samples each. Under some threshold: $\omega_2$ has 18 correct and 2 missed; $\omega_1$ has 14 correct and 6 misclassified. Compute $\alpha$, $\beta$, $1-\beta$, and write the point on the ROC.

p13-practice2-title.name: p13-practice2-title
p13-practice2-title.text: Exercise 2: compute the AUC by pairwise counting

p13-practice2-ctx.name: p13-practice2-ctx
p13-practice2-ctx.text: Work it out yourself first, then press Next for feedback.

p13-practice2-q2.name: p13-practice2-q2
p13-practice2-q2.text: Exercise 2: the values of $\omega_1$ are $1,\ 3,\ 5$ and the values of $\omega_2$ are $2,\ 4,\ 6$. Compute the AUC by pairwise counting.

p13-practice2-lgd.name: p13-practice2-lgd
p13-practice2-lgd.text: Coloured cell = $\omega_2$ larger (win), grey cell = $\omega_1$ larger; the colours match the same-coloured lines above

p14-summary-title.name: p14-summary-title
p14-summary-title.text: The whole KP04: look at overlap, not just the mean gap; but choose the right feature representation

p14-summary-ctx.name: p14-summary-ctx
p14-summary-ctx.text: Left: the conclusions of this unit on one ROC plane; right: what each mark taught (brackets are page numbers).

p14-summary-e0.name: p14-summary-e0
p14-summary-e0.text: One threshold = one point $(\alpha,\ 1-\beta)$ on the ROC plane; $\alpha$ and $\beta$ trade off (2–3)

p14-summary-e1.name: p14-summary-e1
p14-summary-e1.text: Same mean gap 3, large spread ($\sigma=3$): the curve hugs the diagonal, $\mathrm{AUC}=0.760$ (10)

p14-summary-e2.name: p14-summary-e2
p14-summary-e2.text: Small spread ($\sigma=1$): bulges to the upper left, $\mathrm{AUC}=0.983$; $\Phi(\Delta/(\sigma\sqrt2))$ (8, 10)

p14-summary-e3.name: p14-summary-e3
p14-summary-e3.text: Same mean, different spread: with score $x$ the $\mathrm{AUC}=0.50$, with $|x|$ it rises to 0.795 (11)

p14-summary-e4.name: p14-summary-e4
p14-summary-e4.text: $\mathrm{AUC}$ = area under the curve (light purple) = probability that $\omega_2$ is larger in a random pair (6–7)

p14-summary-e5.name: p14-summary-e5
p14-summary-e5.text: The $p$-value is significant (0.011) but the $\mathrm{AUC}$ is only 0.544: the test answers "is there a difference", AUC answers "how separable" (9)

p14-summary-e6.name: p14-summary-e6
p14-summary-e6.text: Next KP: no threshold sweep, compute the score directly from means and variances ⇒ FDR and scatter matrices
